cost.subtitle: Everything we spend, in {currency} — from the visas and jabs before we left to today's coffee. Kept honest so you can judge what a trip like this really takes.

cost.unconverted: Not counted in these totals: {amounts}. This trip’s rate table has no rate for them, so they are shown as they were paid rather than folded into a number that would look right and be wrong. Add the missing rates to the trip’s {file}.

del.backups: This removes the content from this server. Copies kept elsewhere — backups made by whoever runs it, or a version history of the content folder — are not reached by it.
del.doneJournalBody: “{title}” has been deleted. Its address answers “gone” from now on, and the name is not given out to anybody else.
del.doneTripBody: “{title}” and its photographs are gone. The rest of the journal is exactly as it was.
del.expiredBody: A deletion link works once, and for {minutes} minutes. Nothing has been deleted. If you still want to, ask again and a new mail arrives.
del.expiry: Both links above work for {minutes} minutes, and the deletion can be confirmed once.
del.export: This hands you the whole journal as a zip file — private journeys, unpublished drafts and photographs, not only the part strangers can see. You could take it at any time, and this is the last comfortable moment to do it.
del.failed: That did not work, and nothing has been deleted. The link may already have been used, or it may have expired — ask for a new one.
del.footer: Sent by {site} to the address that owns this journal.
del.goneBody: “{title}” was removed by the person who wrote it. The address will not be given to anybody else, so an old link will keep saying exactly this.
del.goneNothingBody: There is nothing here to delete any more. It has already gone.
del.goneTripBody: “{title}” was removed by the person who wrote it. The rest of the journal is still here.
del.journalIntro: {nickname}, something asked {site} to delete “{title}” — the whole journal, at {url}. Nothing has been deleted, and nothing will be until you press the button on the page this mail links to.
del.journalSubject: Delete “{title}”? Nothing has been deleted yet
del.journalTitle: Do you want to delete this journal?
del.journalWhatGoes: {trips} journeys, {days} days and {files} files — {size} in all. Every photograph and every unpublished draft. The address {url} stops working, and the name is not given out to anybody else afterwards.
del.linkNote: Opening the page below deletes nothing. It shows you what is about to go, and asks once more.
del.notYou: If you did not ask for this, do nothing: the links expire on their own and nothing is deleted. It would still be worth having the writing tokens for this journal revoked.
del.pageLead: Read this once before you press anything. There is no undo, and nobody running {site} can put it back.
del.tripIntro: {nickname}, something asked {site} to delete the journey “{title}” out of {journal}. Nothing has been deleted, and nothing will be until you press the button on the page this mail links to.
del.tripSubject: Delete the journey “{title}”? Nothing has been deleted yet
del.tripTitle: Do you want to delete this journey?
del.tripWhatGoes: {days} days and {files} files — {size} in all, the journey's photographs included. Deleting a single day leaves its pictures on disk; deleting a journey does not. The rest of the journal is untouched.
del.usedBody: This link has already been used, so it has done whatever it was going to do. Nothing further will happen if you open it again.

draft.body: Nobody else can read this day: it is absent from the story, the feed, the search index and its own link. Tell your agent to publish it when you are happy with it.

err.crashBody: Not your connection, and not something you did. Try again — if it keeps happening it will be fixed from this side.
err.crashTitle: Something went wrong at our end
err.dayGoneBody: It may have been renamed since the link was sent. The story runs from the first day to the last, so you can find it from there.
err.dayGoneTitle: That day isn’t in this journal
err.linkExpiredBody: Links sent by email expire on purpose, and a deleted record takes its link with it. Ask whoever invited you for a fresh one.
err.notSignedInTitle: You are not signed in here
err.offlineBody: The pages you have already read are still here. Anything new needs a connection — this page will work again as soon as you have one.
err.pageGoneBody: The link is probably older than the page it points at, or it picked up a stray character on the way. Nothing has been lost — everything is still where it was.
err.tripGoneBody: It was taken down or renamed. The other trips are all still where they were.
err.tripGoneTitle: That trip isn’t here any more
err.unknownUserBody: Every journal here lives at the name of the person who writes it. Check the link you were sent — if you typed it in, one letter is usually all it takes.
err.unknownUserTitle: There is no journal at this address

landing.hero: A travel journal your agent writes for you.
landing.instruction: Guide me through creating my own travel journal, following the overview at {docUrl} and the full guide at {agentUrl}. You will need an email address I control.
landing.lede: Your journal is markdown and photographs in a folder you own. You read it in a browser. An agent writes it — you hand it a link and an email address.
landing.metaDescription: Markdown and photographs in a folder you own. Read it in a browser; write it through an agent.
landing.metaTitle: {name} — a travel journal your agent writes
landing.noEditor: There is no editing interface, and there won’t be one. The agent is the editor.
landing.publicNone: No journals yet. Copy content/example to content/<your-name> and reload.
landing.readersBody: You don’t need any of this. Follow the link you were sent.
landing.selfHostBody: A VPS, Node and Caddy, one deploy script. A public journal needs no database. AGPL-3.0.
landing.step1Body: It reads the guide there — every call, with examples.
landing.step2: Give it an email address you control
landing.step2Body: The one that owns the journal. No other address can write.
landing.step3: Pass back the code that arrives
landing.step3Body: It can then write for seven days. Everything it writes waits as a draft.

me.agentBody: Press the button below for a prompt to hand an agent — it already knows what to do with it.
me.agentTitle: To write, or to start a new trip
me.askOwner: There is nothing to fill in here — this journal keeps no guestbook. The link they send you is what lets you in.
me.askOwnerNamed: There is nothing to fill in here — this journal keeps no guestbook. It is kept by {name}: the link {name} sends you is what lets you in.
me.detailsBody: Your name, language and postal address are yours to change. Nothing else on this site can be edited here — the journal is written by an agent.
me.handoverCreate: Get a key and the instructions
me.handoverFailed: The key could not be made. Try again.
me.handoverReady: Paste all of this into your agent. The key in it stops working at {time}, so do it now — after that, press the button again.
me.handoverWarning: This key becomes a seven-day key to write in your journal, the first time your agent uses it. Give it to an agent you started yourself, never to a page or a chat somebody else sent you.
me.inviteBuddyBody: Only for the people who were actually on the trip. Once you say yes, they can write to that trip and add to it, the same as you can. Do not put this one in a group chat.
me.inviteBuddyTitle: A link for someone to write
me.inviteGuestBody: Safe to send to the family. It lets somebody ask to read this journal, and nothing more — they see nothing until you say yes.
me.inviteGuestTitle: A link for someone to read
me.keysBody: One line per key you have handed out. Revoking one stops it at once — the agent holding it can no longer write, and nothing it already wrote is touched.
me.keysHandover: A key waiting to be picked up
me.keysTitle: Keys that can write here now
me.nothing: Nothing yet. Ask whoever sent you here to invite you.
me.ownerNoTrips: Nothing yet — there are no trips in this journal so far. A new trip is written by an agent; the prompt it needs is further down this page.
me.peopleBody: Links for other people, and the list of who has asked. Neither link lets anybody in on its own — whoever opens one leaves their name and waits for you.
me.peopleTitle: Inviting someone, and who reads along
me.signInBody: If you have read this journal before, sign in with the same email address and we will send you a six-digit code.
me.signInSent: If that address has access, a code is on its way. It works for {minutes} minutes.
me.signInWrong: That code did not work. Check it, or ask for a new one.
me.signOutBody: This ends your session on this device. To come back you will need a new code by email, so only sign out if you are on somebody else's computer.
me.signOutFailed: That did not work, and you are still signed in. Try again.
me.signinExpired: That link had already been used, so it did not let you in. This is common and it is not something you did wrong: mail providers often open links in a message before you do. Ask for a fresh code below and it will work.
me.signinThrottled: That was a lot of attempts in a short time. Wait a few minutes and try again, or ask for a fresh code below.
me.strangerBody: If somebody sent you a link to this journal, follow it. To be added properly, ask them to invite you.
me.strangerBodyNamed: This journal is kept by {name}. If somebody sent you a link to it, follow it. To be added properly, ask {name} to invite you.
me.title: Your access
me.tokenBody: A key from here — or a code you read out — becomes a key that works for seven days, on this journal and nothing else. It can write days, and it can put one on the site when you ask it to; everything it writes waits as a draft until you do. It is the whole of your editing, which is why it goes to somebody you trust and never into a group chat.
me.tokenWarning: None of it is the same as being signed in here. Reading your journal in this browser cannot change it — a key can, until it expires, and anyone holding one can use it.

test.title: Test content — this is not a real day
trips.emptyOwnerBody: This journal is empty. You do not start a trip here — there is no form, and there never will be. Press the button below for a prompt to hand an agent, and it will set the first one up.
trips.emptyOwnerFilteredBody: You have a trip, but its trip.md marks it `listed: false` — which keeps it out of this list too, not only the sitemap and the switcher. Set `listed: true` there to see it here.
trips.hiddenBody: There is nothing here you can read. Journeys in this journal may be private — ask {name} for an invite link, or sign in below with the address they invited.
trips.hiddenSignedInBody: You are signed in, but nothing here is shared with your address yet. Ask {name} to widen it.
trips.malformedIdMismatch: its id does not match the folder name — the two must be the same
trips.malformedIntro: These folders have a problem in their trip.md and will appear once it is fixed. Only you can see this.
trips.malformedIntro.one: This folder has a problem in its trip.md and will appear once it is fixed. Only you can see this.
trips.malformedInvalidId: its id is not valid — lowercase letters, numbers and dashes only
trips.malformedMissingFields: it needs a title and start and end dates written as 2027-04-01
trips.malformedMissingId: it has no id, and the id must match the folder name
trips.malformedNoFile: there is no trip.md in it
trips.malformedUnparseable: its frontmatter could not be read
trips.noEntriesYet: No days written yet — this one hasn’t happened.
trips.subtitle: Everywhere we’ve been, and where we’re going next.

welcome.addressNote: Your journal lives at {url}. This is the only mail that carries the address.
welcome.drafts: You can see what is waiting at any time — your agent can list the drafts, and reading one back is how you check it did not invent anything. When you are happy with one, tell your agent to publish it; that is the whole of it, and nothing goes up until you say so.
welcome.draftsHeading: Nothing an agent writes is published
welcome.draftsRule: Everything written into this journal by an agent arrives as a draft and stays invisible to readers until you say it can go up. That is so you can read a day back before anyone else does — your agent publishes it when you tell it to, and not before.
welcome.footer: Sent by {site} because a journal was created for this address.
welcome.intro: {nickname}, “{title}” now exists on {site} and it is yours. This is the only mail that carries its address, so keep it.
welcome.linkNote: That button signs you in, so you can see drafts and private journeys — don’t forward this mail if you only meant to share the address. It works once; afterwards, and any time later, the journal is at {url} and you can ask for a fresh sign-in code there.
welcome.private: It is private: it appears on no list on this server and asks search engines not to index it, so the only people who will find it are the ones you send the address to. Whether a particular journey can be read is set on the journey itself.
welcome.public: It is public: it is listed on this server’s own index and search engines may index it. Each journey still decides for itself whether anyone can read it, and a new one starts out private.
welcome.subject: Your journal is ready — {title}
welcome.title: Your journal is ready
welcome.token: Ask your agent to start at {guide}. It will ask this server to mail a six-digit code to {email} — this address, and no other — and that code becomes a token that can write for seven days.
welcome.tokenHeading: If you want to write to it later
